summary: LLM inference costs are driven almost entirely by token volume, where output tokens typically cost 3-8x more than input tokens (flagship models charge $2-3/M input and $10-15/M output). A disciplined combination of prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints routinely cuts API spend by 40-80% with minimal quality impact. The highest-leverage move is prompt caching (up to 90% savings on repeated prefixes with no output change), but optimization is not worth the engineering time for very low-volume workloads (e.g. under ~$200/month spend).

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix caching)
techniques.description: Providers store the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, long context) so the static portion isn't reprocessed on each call. The saving is structural with zero change to model output. The key engineering task is ordering prompts so the static part stays static at the front.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens (typically 50-90% of input bill on repetitive prefixes)
techniques.example: Move your 2,000-token system prompt and few-shot examples to the very start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI charge the cached-input rate (often ~10% of normal) on the repeated prefix.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Instead of exact-string matching, embed incoming queries and return a cached response when a prior query is semantically similar above a tuned similarity threshold. Highly effective on conversational and FAQ-style workloads, but requires careful threshold management to avoid returning confidently wrong answers for near-miss queries.
techniques.savings: 30-50% cost reduction on conversational workloads (45% cache hit rate reported); studies show 41-80% cost reduction with strategic cache boundaries
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache with a 0.9 cosine-similarity threshold so 'how do I cancel my subscription?' reuses the cached answer for 'cancel my plan how?'.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: A deterministic cache keyed on the exact request string (plus params). The cheapest and safest layer in a multi-tier caching strategy, catching identical repeated requests before any embedding or model call is made.
techniques.savings: 100% cost savings on each cache hit (hit rate varies by workload)
techniques.example: Key an in-memory or Redis cache on a hash of the full prompt so identical requests return instantly with no API call.

techniques.name: Model Routing (tiered model selection)
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, reserving flagship models only for hard queries. Budget-tier models can cost ~16x less than flagship for identical token counts, so routing the bulk of traffic to cheaper models yields large savings.
techniques.savings: Up to 10-16x cost difference on routed traffic; teams route ~70% to budget, 25% to mid-tier, 5% to flagship
techniques.example: Send simple classification and FAQ queries to GPT-4o-mini ($0.15/$0.60) and escalate only complex reasoning tasks to GPT-4o or Claude Opus.

techniques.name: Output Token Constraints
techniques.description: Cap and shape output since output tokens cost 3-8x more than input. Set max_tokens, request concise or structured (JSON/enum) responses, and use stop sequences to prevent runaway generations. This directly attacks the most expensive part of the bill.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Answer in one sentence' or use structured outputs with an enum to stop the model padding responses.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce input tokens by trimming redundant instructions, compressing context, and using automated compressors (e.g. LLMLingua) that drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning. Useful when long contexts dominate the input bill.
techniques.savings: ~30% input token reduction (up to 50%+ with aggressive compression)
techniques.example: Run LLMLingua over retrieved RAG context to strip filler tokens before sending the prompt, cutting input length ~30% with negligible quality loss.

techniques.name: Retrieval / Context Pruning (RAG optimization)
techniques.description: Send only the most relevant retrieved chunks instead of stuffing large contexts. Tighter top-k retrieval and reranking shrink input tokens and often improve answer quality by reducing distraction.
techniques.savings: 20-60% input token reduction depending on prior over-retrieval
techniques.example: Reduce RAG retrieval from top-20 chunks to a reranked top-3, cutting context tokens dramatically while keeping answer accuracy.

techniques.name: Request Batching & Async / Batch APIs
techniques.description: Group non-latency-sensitive requests into batch endpoints that providers discount heavily, and combine multiple small tasks into one call to amortize fixed prompt overhead.
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk summarization jobs via OpenAI's Batch API to get a 50% discount versus synchronous calls.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream outputs and stop generation as soon as the needed answer is produced, avoiding paying for trailing tokens; combine with stop sequences for structured extraction tasks.
techniques.savings: 10-30% output token reduction on tasks with natural early stop points
techniques.example: Stream a JSON extraction and close the connection once the closing brace is received to avoid paying for extra tokens.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores embeddings of queries and returns cached responses for semantically similar requests, supporting exact and similarity-based matching.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; you pay for your own vector store/embedding infra)

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store offering exact-match and vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses via RediSearch and the redis-llm integrations, used for multi-tier caching strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (self-hosted open source); Redis Cloud paid tiers scale with memory/usage

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost tracking, caching, and rate limiting via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (limited requests); paid plans from ~$20/month plus usage-based tiers

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source proxy/SDK that gives a unified OpenAI-compatible API across 100+ providers, with built-in caching, model routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); LiteLLM Enterprise with SSO/support quoted on request

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM response caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic) plus abstractions for routing, retrieval, and prompt management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); LangSmith observability has a free tier and paid plans from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression toolkit that uses a small language model to drop low-information tokens, compressing prompts up to ~20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway routing requests across many model providers with automatic fallbacks, price comparison, and the ability to route to the cheapest capable model.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use the router; pay per-token at (often marked-up or at-cost) model rates

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic and simple caching, model routing, load balancing, retries, and observability through a single proxy endpoint.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (limited logs/requests); paid plans from ~$49/month plus usage

tools.name: Finout
tools.description: FinOps/cloud cost management platform that tracks and attributes LLM token spend by model and team to identify optimization opportunities.

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching and reorder prompts so the static system prompt and few-shot examples sit at the front of every request (up to 90% savings on repeated prefixes, no quality change).
Set max_tokens and request concise/structured output to cut the expensive output-token bill by roughly 50%.
Add an exact-match response cache (Redis or in-memory) keyed on the full prompt hash to eliminate duplicate API calls for free.
Route the bulk of simple requests (~70%) to a budget model like GPT-4o-mini and reserve flagship models only for hard queries — up to a 16x cost difference on routed traffic.
Instrument spend with Helicone or LiteLLM to see per-model/per-route costs before investing engineering time (and skip heavy optimization if you spend under ~$200/month).
